subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Biomarkers HE4, ROMA Index and Dysgerminoma

steps.tx: The epididymal secretory protein **human epididymis protein 4** serves as a sensitive serum biomarker for epithelial ovarian carcinoma. Unlike CA-125, HE4 is rarely elevated in benign gynaecological conditions like endometriosis, uterine adenomyosis, or pelvic inflammatory disease. This distinct specificity provides superior diagnostic utility when evaluating premenopausal pelvic masses.
steps.say: Human epididymis protein 4 distinguishes ovarian malignancy from benign endometriosis with superior specificity.

rows: Falsely elevated due to low clearance

steps.tx: Stratification algorithms combine biomarkers into the **ROMA predictive model**, standing for Risk of Ovarian Malignancy Algorithm. By integrating serum concentrations of HE4 and CA-125 with menopausal status, ROMA generates a percentage probability score of harboring epithelial malignancy. High-risk classification accurately directs surgical triage toward specialized gynaecological oncological centers.
steps.say: The ROMA algorithm calculates the statistical probability of ovarian malignancy using HE4 and CA-125.

steps.tx: The most common malignant ovarian germ cell tumor in adolescents and young women is **ovarian dysgerminoma**, morphologically identical to testicular seminoma. It typically arises in the second and third decades of life and may be associated with gonadal dysgenesis such as Swyer syndrome. Most cases present as unilateral solid encapsulated adnexal masses.
steps.say: Dysgerminoma is the most common malignant germ cell tumor in young females and resembles seminoma.

steps.tx: The gross **dysgerminoma** specimen is a solid, lobulated mass with a fleshy, cream-coloured cut surface, closely echoing testicular seminoma under the knife and the microscope alike. It usually affects adolescents and young women and can arise within dysgenetic gonads. Rapid growth may stretch the capsule and cause pain or torsion. Lactate dehydrogenase released by the tumour cells later serves as its circulating marker.
steps.say: Dysgerminoma is the most common malignant germ cell tumour in young females and resembles seminoma. Its fleshy solid cut surface matches that resemblance.

vis.alt: Gross specimen of an ovarian dysgerminoma sliced open to reveal a lobulated, solid, fleshy tan cut surface with a smooth outer capsule.
vis.caption: The cut tumour looks like its testicular twin seminoma, a solid fleshy lobulated mass rather than a cystic ovarian neoplasm. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: The reliable circulating biomarker for diagnosing and monitoring dysgerminoma is **lactate dehydrogenase elevation**. Dysgerminoma cells actively release total LDH and its specific isoenzymes one and two during accelerated cellular turnover. Serum human chorionic gonadotropin may also be mildly elevated if syncytiotrophoblastic giant cells are interspersed throughout the tumor.
steps.say: Serum lactate dehydrogenase serves as the key diagnostic marker and monitoring tool in dysgerminoma.

steps.tx: Histopathological examination reveals uniform sheets and nests of **polygonal dysgerminoma cells** with clear glycogen-filled cytoplasm and central vesicular nuclei containing prominent nucleoli. These malignant cell nests are partitioned by delicate fibrous septa densely infiltrated by mature T-lymphocytes. Granulomatous reactions with multinucleated giant cells frequently accompany this lymphoid infiltrate.
steps.say: Dysgerminoma features sheets of glycogen-rich clear cells intersected by fibrous septa with lymphocytes.

steps.tx: Because the majority of patients present at stage one and desire future childbearing, **fertility sparing surgery** represents the standard management. Unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy with preservation of the contralateral ovary and uterus provides excellent oncological control. Routine biopsy of a normal contralateral ovary is avoided due to the risk of mechanical adhesions.
steps.say: Fertility-sparing unilateral adnexectomy is the preferred surgical option for stage one dysgerminoma.

steps.tx: Dysgerminoma displays exceptional sensitivity to ionizing radiation and systemically administered **platinum combination chemotherapy**. The first-line regimen consists of bleomycin, etoposide, and cisplatin, abbreviated as BEP. Administered over three to four cycles, BEP achieves long-term overall cure rates approaching ninety-five percent, even in patients with metastatic disease.
steps.say: Combination chemotherapy with bleomycin, etoposide, and cisplatin achieves exceptional cure rates.

steps.tx: Post-treatment surveillance involves systematic clinical examination, pelvic ultrasonography, and serial **biomarker monitoring**. Serum LDH levels and CA-125 are assessed every two to three months for the first two years. Rapid resurgence in serum LDH indicates asymptomatic disease recurrence, allowing prompt salvage therapeutic intervention before bulky recurrence develops.
steps.say: Serial monitoring of serum LDH enables early detection and successful salvage of disease recurrence.
